title: Token-path SLI decomposition and circuit-state chronicle
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a set of reliable, low-cardinality metrics and dashboards that decompose token-path SLI failures across region, shard, and priority and surface circuit-breaker state transitions and load-shedding signals. This ticket covers the instrumentation spec, metric naming, exemplar sampling decisions, dashboard panels, alert thresholds, and a synthetic harness to validate behavior under multi-region failover and admission-shed events. Goal: give SREs and runtime owners a single-pane view to diagnose why token-level latency SLOs are missed and to correlate those misses with circuit opens, admission rejections, and KV cache behavior.
acceptance_criteria: New metrics deployed to runtime and ingestion pipeline: token_admit_latency_ms (histogram), token_service_latency_ms (histogram), token_admit_rate (counter), token_shed_count (counter), kv_cache_hit_ratio (gauge), circuit_state (gauge: 0=closed,1=open), circuit_open_reason (label) with region/shard/priority labels where cardinality-controlled

Grafana dashboard 'Token-Path Chronicle' with panels: SLO decomposition by region/shard/priority, Admit Path Waterfall, Circuit State Timeline, Shedding Heatmap, KV hit vs latency scatter, Batch-size distribution and its impact on tail latency

Exemplar traces emitted for p95+ latency samples with trace IDs linking to runtime span traces (sampling rate 1 in 1000 by default, configurable), and exemplar fields include request_id, model_variant, sequence_length
PagerDuty alerts created for sustained SLO burn-rate >3x over 1h and circuit_open_rate >10% for >5m; thresholds documented in Confluence runbook

Synthetic runner scenarios implemented and run: low-latency normal traffic, multi-region failover (region-A down), admission saturation (burst to 2x capacity), and KV cold-start; results committed as CSV/benchmarks and linked from dashboard
Runbook updated with triage steps, mitigation playbook (fallback model variant, regional failover steps, admission throttle adjustments), and post-incident RCA template
tasks: Design metric naming and label set — balance SLI usefulness vs cardinality
Implement runtime instrumentation changes and expose metrics via telemetry endpoint
Add exemplar logic to latency histograms and wire to trace system
Create Grafana dashboard with required panels and templating variables (region, shard, priority, model_variant)
Define and create alerts in Alertmanager and map to PagerDuty
Build synthetic runner jobs (k6 + small harness) to exercise scenarios and upload artifacts
Run load test and validate SLO decomposition and circuit-state correlation
Write Confluence runbook and link PRs/dashboards
updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting with Runtime, Observability, and SRE. Agreed on primary SLO: per-tenant rolling 30d p99 token admission latency target and per-route p95 token service latency target.

2026-02-18: Decided cardinality policy: labels allowed - region, shard_group (coarse), priority (serving tier), model_family; customer_id will NOT be a primary label to avoid cardinality explosion. Per-tenant SLOs deferred to follow-up ticket.

2026-02-25: Prototype histogram + exemplar emitted from admission path. Initial exemplar payload too large; trimmed to include only request_id, seq_len, and sample_reason. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1734

2026-03-02: Design review feedback from Observability: move from high-cardinality shard_id to shard_group (e.g., group by physical pool of GPUs) and add 'admit_bucket' label (fast/slow) for cheaper rollups. Implemented in branch and running in staging.

2026-03-08: Synthetic runner scenario 'region-failover' executed. Observed correlated increase in token_admit_latency_ms and circuit_state flips in secondary region. Collected CSV artifacts and added preliminary dashboard panels for visualization. Finding: KV cache cold starts amplify p99 by ~1.6x during failover.

2026-03-10: Security review request submitted (see Confluence link). Not blocking for metric rollout but required before releasing runbook to customers. Scheduling follow-up with Security on 2026-03-15.
